hold_text: Routed for a human merge because R5 cannot certify src/runtime/decision_subject.py, src/runtime/work_decisions.py or src/web/api/routers/work.py as Tier-1 BY PATH -- not because the work is Tier-2 or Tier-3 in substance, and no Tier-2/3 permission is being requested. The reviewer's check is one question: does this diff touch a WRITER, an ORDER PATH, or a CONFIG? It does not. The only behaviour change is what a READ route publishes about a decision request, plus a new pure module with no I/O beyond reading four JSON registers and the work-object directory that the same route already reads.
why: MI-258. A decision request kept rendering on the operator's Workflow page as work waiting on THEM for more than a day after its subject was deleted (DR-20260908-CLEAR-THE-LOUD-TRADE-PRIORITISATION-ROW asks whether to remove an OPEN-ITEMS row that left the file on 2026-09-09 in ba5fccc1a, #11509). Tier-1 by the canonical doc's own list -- 'observability / read paths, retrieving + analyzing state'. NO order path, NO journal writer, NO config/**, NO risk caps, NO deploy/ or unit file, NO new write surface (the decision inbox's write route is untouched and this does not widen it). Nothing in it can place, modify or refuse an order. THE MEASUREMENT THAT SHAPED IT: over ALL 26 decision_requests across the 21 objects that carry any (of 710 work objects, at de46c805e), a prose scan for ids and paths flagged 4 subjects as vanished and THREE WERE FALSE (75%) -- one an id truncated by a YAML line wrap mid-token whose real row is live, two sentence-ending periods captured into paths whose files both exist -- and 13 of 26 carried no extractable reference at all. So the subject is a DECLARED typed field and is never inferred from prose: a 75% false-positive rate on a signal that REMOVES a question from the operator's screen would hide live decisions. Four states, never collapsed, registered with collapsed-state-guard: subject_live / subject_gone / subject_unknown (we could not look) / subject_undeclared (25 of 26 today -- pooling it into unknown would report a 96% resolution failure for work never attempted). Every refusal is mutation-tested and each protects the same direction: an unreadable or missing register grades unknown never gone; a partial work-store read may say live but never gone; a ref that is a strict prefix of a live id grades unknown; pull_request and branch refuse rather than fetching, because network on an API request path is the wedge class this repo has paid for twice; a raising resolver grades unknown; and `actionable` withdraws only on `gone`. One mutation caught a VACUOUS TEST OF MY OWN -- the network-kinds test parametrized over the constant under test, so emptying it made the test SKIP rather than FAIL -- now rewritten with the kinds spelled out. `lifecycle: done` on the parent is deliberately NOT consulted, per the row's own instruction that it is evidence and not the test, even though the confirmed instance would have been suppressible on it alone. 32 tests pass. ⚠️ tests/test_work_router.py and tests/test_work_decisions.py could NOT be run in this container (fastapi uninstallable, repeated PyPI read timeouts), so CI is the first place they run -- stated rather than implied, since they exercise the route this diff changes. ⚠️ The SPA render is a SECOND REPO and is not here: until ict-trader-dashboard reads `actionable`, the operator's list is unchanged and the fix is producer-side only.
